newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong no base for destabilising China - Tung.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong no base for destabilising China - Tung.

text.p: Hong Kong's future chief executive Tung Chee-Hwa said on Monday he would not allow Hong Kong to become a base for destabilising China.
But Tung, who takes over from Governor Chris Patten when the British pull out on June 30, said he would allow demonstrations under Chinese rule as long as they were legal, peaceful and orderly.
Asked by Britain's Channel Four if he was prepared to imprison people for political views, he said: "I will not permit Hong Kong to become a base to destabilise China.

"This is not acceptable to a large group of people in Hong Kong because it is not in Hong Kong's interest to permit this. Certainly it is not in China's interest to do this. This cannot be permitted."
Critics have accused Tung of being a puppet of the Beijing government and human rights activists fear a major clampdown with civil rights being rolled back.
Tung said demonstrations would be permitted in Hong Kong after the handover "as long as they are peaceful, lawful and orderly."
The former shipping tycoon insisted that human rights were not a monopoly of the west.

"We all want human rights, I want human rights, I care passionately about human rights but each country has its own priorities. For China it is a question of moving the country ahead, making it more prosperous."
On June 4, tens of thousands of Hong Kong people congregated in a local park to honour the victims of Beijing's bloody 1989 crackdown in Tiananmen Square.
Tung argued it was time to look forward and not back.
"Let us put aside the baggage of June 4, let us look into the future, build a new and better Hong Kong for ourselves and our children," he said.
Tung went to school at Bournemouth in southern England and then on to university at Liverpool.
He said: "I have benefited from western education but I am Chinese and I treasure very much the Chinese values which were instilled in me by my parents and grandparents."
Ending the interview on a lighter note, he pledged that he would fly to Britain to watch Liverpool Football Club if they got into the soccer Cup Final.
